nodes.label: KajarTick Audio Feedback
nodes.rationale: Uses an isolated AVAudioPlayer pool so button clicks sound outside active game audio sessions.

nodes.label: Solo Guided Practice Mission
nodes.rationale: Empowers young Balinese to learn gamelan on their own schedule without requiring standing sekaa membership or risking beginner embarrassment.

nodes.label: No-Fail Practice Mode
nodes.rationale: Removes scoring and fail state while waiting indefinitely for the correct key, directly addressing fear of failure.

nodes.label: Inharmonic Bronze Spectral Fingerprinting
nodes.rationale: Bronze metallophones produce inharmonic partials (~1, 2.76, 5.42, 8.91x), making fundamental-finding ineffective; a 120-element L2-normalised spectral shape vector is used instead.

nodes.label: Dual STFT Window Strategy
nodes.rationale: 1024-sample STFT provides temporal precision for onset detection, while 4096-sample FFT provides frequency precision for spectral fingerprinting.

nodes.label: Vision Which Key Audio When Split
nodes.norm_label: vision which key audio when split
nodes.rationale: Vision identifies keys by spatial location without pitch confusion, while audio supplies millisecond timing and strike confirmation.

nodes.label: Audio Session Measurement Mode
nodes.rationale: .playAndRecord with .measurement mode disables iOS AGC and echo cancellation which would corrupt onset detection and pitch analysis.

nodes.label: Support Not Replacement Rationale
nodes.rationale: Technology stays in a support role to lower the initial barrier before a teacher or community, never claiming to replace human instruction.

nodes.label: Key Index Addressing Convention
nodes.rationale: Every village in Bali tunes differently, so notes and kotekan address bilah strictly by index rather than pitch or physical position.

nodes.label: Timing Judgement Model
nodes.rationale: Generous timing windows (Perfect ±60ms, Good ±120ms, Late/Early ±200ms) accommodate beginner tempo before tightening.

nodes.label: Peripheral Screen Visibility Design
nodes.rationale: Players standing over instruments cannot read small phone screens, mitigated by large peripheral overlay shapes, audio cues carrying timing, and external exhibition mirroring.

nodes.label: Wired QuickTime Mirroring
nodes.rationale: Exhibition display uses wired cable to QuickTime on Mac rather than AirPlay to avoid venue Wi-Fi latency/instability and capture simultaneous recording.

nodes.label: Left-Hand Key Damping
nodes.rationale: Gangsa requires left-hand pinching to damp ringing keys; v1 teaches this visually in practice mode but deliberately does not score it to avoid discouraging beginners.

nodes.label: Single Bundled Profile Scope Decision
nodes.rationale: Bundles one calibrated profile for the owned gangsa to achieve a 15-second setup while retaining per-instrument calibration architecture for village tunings.

nodes.label: Lottie Package Dependency
nodes.rationale: Only third-party dependency; used solely to play two dotLottie interlock onboarding animations.

nodes.label: MainActor Default Isolation
nodes.rationale: SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION set to MainActor so UI code is main-actor isolated by default while heavy computation is explicitly nonisolated or actors.

nodes.label: Periodic Comb Bilah Detection
nodes.rationale: Fits one periodic comb of N teeth (pitch + phase) instead of finding N bars independently; keys on structural periodicity rather than brightness or colour.

nodes.label: Single Camera Session Pattern
nodes.rationale: Maintains one session and one preview layer re-parented per screen to eliminate a measured 9-second main-thread stall caused by per-screen layers.

nodes.label: Audio Cue Guidance Layer
nodes.rationale: Metronome click, reference tones (calibrated sample one beat ahead), and feedback tones allow users to follow patterns primarily by ear as gamelan is traditionally transmitted.
